chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hafs ibn Amr, Abu Muhammad, the announcer of Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
I saw upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he was praying in the garden, a quince-coloured Khazz cloak.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (a title for Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الرَّوْضَة: The garden (a specific location mentioned in the narration)
key_terms.جُبَّةَ خَزٍّ: A cloak made of Khazz (a type of coarse wool or fabric)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam wear while praying in the garden according to this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Sahih al-Kulayni, highlights the modesty and simplicity of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) by depicting him in a simple woolen cloak (Jubbah Khazz) during prayer in the Rawdah. It serves as a practical model for the Shia tradition, emphasizing that spiritual devotion is not contingent upon luxurious attire but rather on inner piety and humility. The specific mention of 'Safarjaliyyah' (a type of coarse or specific wool) underscores the preference for natural, unadorned fabrics among the Imams.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hafs Bin Amro Abu Muhammad the announcer of Ali Bin Yaqteen who said,
‘I saw upon Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was Praying in the garden, a quince-coloured Khazz cloak’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Hafs ibn ‘Umar (‘Amr) abu Muhammad Mu’adhdhin Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “

I saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, performing Salat (prayer) in al-Rawdah and wore a jubbah (gown) of al-Khazz (garments made of skin or fur of an animal that lives in water) of the color of quince.’”
